main_body: A tall palm tree: a thin vertical brown ringed trunk about 5px wide and 40+ rows tall, under a small dark-green frond crown with a light-green heart at the top
top_band: At x=16, rows 2-6 are light green (L=142), but this is only the small central heart of the crown. Below it are dark frond rows 7-17 (L about 20-55), then the trunk.
evidence: The largest volume is the trunk, a straight column drawn face-on in alternating 2-row bark bands (L=46/73). It has no visible top surface because the crown hides it. The only light surface is a small 6px-wide patch at the centre of a dark, mostly flat radial frond fan, so the top is visible on only a small part. There is no distinct front-edge line, eave shadow or recessed front. Strictly, it reads as a front elevation of a trunk with a hat, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. The fronds use about 3-4 dark greens with no leaf clumps or per-leaf highlights. The trunk is a uniform brown strip with a repeating 2-row stripe pattern and almost no grain. The outlines are tinted dark green or brown (0% neutral), which is fine, but the piece is much thinner and flatter than the lush, textured Beodeul trees.
